title: fix: a userfile is readable only by callers every owning record permits (part of #905; #941)
body:
## Summary

**This PR is a PARTIAL fix of #905 and does not close its disclosure.** A MASTER_DATA_EDIT holder can still clear a protecting value or delete the owning record and then read the file (see "Residual F5 findings"). That bypass is tracked as #920 and is an unresolved security dependency: the F5 deferral was not acceptance of it.

`GET /api/files/userfiles/{fileName}` served any userfile to any authenticated caller who held its stored name, and `force_serve_as=picture` also wrote a derivative for them. A userfile is now readable only by a caller whom every record referencing it admits (F1-F4). The write paths are unchanged (F5); the shopping-list page (F6) is a separate PR.

## Root cause

`FilesApiController::GROUP_READ_PERMISSIONS['userfiles']` was `null` ("open"), and nothing links a file to its owner except the text of a `userfield_values.value`. The stored name was the only secret and it survived permission removal and owner deletion.

## What changed

- New `controllers/Users/UserfileOwnerPolicy.php`; `FilesApiController::CheckGroupReadPermission` calls it for the new `OWNER_GOVERNED` group marker, so it runs before `GetStoredName` / `Read` (no bytes, no derivative for a refused caller).
- OpenAPI: `GET /files/{group}/{fileName}` gains a `403` (inline `ApiError`, the pattern the neighbouring operations use) and a description of the rule. Hunk inside that operation only.
- Changelog line; one sentence in `docs/security-sweep.md` (the historical "only two land on null" paragraph).
- Tests: new `tests/Pgsql/UserfileOwnerReadTest.php` (registered last in `storagefiles`); changes to existing tests listed below.

## Behaviour decided

Quoting the maintainer (2026-10-13): F1 "ADMIN only ... Treat an unresolved owner as an orphan only after checking all supported reference forms." F2 "every referencing owner must permit access. Deduplicate references. An unresolved or denied owner prevents access. Authorize the original file before reading or creating a picture derivative." F3 "deny unless an explicit policy permits access ... Preserve intentional non-exposure, including for administrators." F3' definitions (`userfields`, `userentities`) are ADMIN only, as an explicit named exception in the policy; `EntityReadPolicy` is untouched. F4 "Apply the existing self-read exception to the user's own files, subject to F2".

Rule: access is the intersection over the distinct `(entity, object_id)` references.

| Reference | Admits |
|---|---|
| none (orphan) | ADMIN |
| record does not exist / key not canonical (`01`, `abc`) / entity with a read policy but no lookup here (`label_*`, `print_*`, all ADMIN in `EntityReadPolicy`, so this equals applying their policy) | ADMIN |
| one of the 12 views (see below), row found by `id` | the view's `EntityReadPolicy` permission; a view row that is gone is unresolved: ADMIN |
| `userentity-*` | MASTER_DATA_EDIT |
| `users` | USERS_READ, or that user themselves |
| entity with a non-null `EntityReadPolicy::PERMISSIONS` row | that permission |
| `roles`, `mqtt_product_entities` (plain tables, integer id) | USERS_READ, STOCK_VIEW |
| `userfields`, `userentities` | ADMIN |
| `api_keys` (even if the key row is gone) | nobody |
| entity with no `EntityReadPolicy` row at all | nobody |

ADMIN is checked literally: a caller holding every leaf but ADMIN cannot read an orphan. A derivative is not a file in its own right. Any requested or referenced name is reduced, by stripping every `__downscaledto<h|auto>x<w|auto>` suffix (`FilesService::DerivativeChain` / `RootOf`), to its root original. The root must have a reference (an unreferenced root is ADMIN only, whatever references its derivatives have), every reference to any name in the chain must admit the caller, and for the `userfiles` group `GetStoredName` derives only from the root, so no name with two suffixes is created there (every other group derives from the name as asked, as on master). A value naming a derivative can therefore only narrow. A value whose `userfields` definition row is gone is an unresolved reference (ADMIN). Row ids use the full INTEGER range. Every ownership refusal is the same `403` with body `{"error_message":"Permission missing: USERFILE_OWNER_READ"}` (a fixed name that is not a real permission), including for a name that does not exist, because authorization precedes the existence check. A permitted caller asking for a referenced file with no bytes still gets `404`.

Owner lookup follows `GenericEntityApiController::GetObject`: the twelve views by `id` (`OWNER_VIEWS`); `stock` is keyed by `stock_id` (text), `label_printer_status` by `printer_id`, `userentity-<name>` by `userobjects.id` joined to `userentities.name`, everything else by integer `id`. The table is an explicit constant; table and column names never come from stored data.

### Reference forms found (F1)
1. `base64(stored) + '_' + base64(display)` — written by `userfieldsform.js:69-70`; git history shows the same format since the component was introduced.
2. bare `base64(stored)` — `PUT /api/userfields` accepts any string; the existing canary test (`CustomEntityGenericReadsTest`) writes this form.
No other writer exists: `DemoDataGeneratorService` writes only text values; the importer and devtools fixtures contain no file values. Matching decodes the part before the first `_` with the same non-strict `base64_decode` that `ServeFile` applies to the URL, so padding-less, dropped-bit and stray-character variants are references too. All field types count, not only `file`/`image`.

## Verification

Before the fix (round 0, new tests only, `storagefiles`): `Tests: 88, Assertions: 518, Failures: 30`, e.g. `a caller holding nothing: expected a refusal / Failed asserting that 200 is identical to 403`. Round 1 tests on ebf04429: `Tests: 98, Assertions: 880, Errors: 1, Failures: 9`, including `testReferencingADerivativeNeverWidensWhoMayReadIt` (`STOCK_VIEW alone, by the derivative name: expected a refusal / Failed asserting that 200 is identical to 403`), `testAValueWhoseDefinitionIsGoneIsAnUnresolvedReference` and the `roles` case (`403 is identical to 200`). The one error was the new max-id test failing in its own cleanup.

After the fix, final head 96f293e5, all nine phases: `storagefiles` OK (98 tests, 917 assertions); `rbac` OK (114, 1293); `householdpages` OK (90, 697; includes the unchanged `CustomEntityGenericReadsTest` canary); `stockpages` OK (73, 674); `labelapi` OK (158, 2709); `contract` exit 0 (28 tests); `openapidocument` OK (15, 36); `openapisecurity` OK (11, 86); `wirecontract` OK (135, 4069). Vale ran in the pre-commit hook: 0 new findings.

Existing tests changed: `StorageFilesTest::testReadingAGroupWithoutItsPermissionServesNothing` inverted (403 for a zero-grant caller, 200 for ADMIN); setup only (grant `ADMIN`, assertions untouched) in `testWhatIsServedInlineAndWhatIsHandedOverAsADownload`, `testServedFilesMatchTheirDocumentedResponse`, `testNonTextBytesRoundTripByteForByte`, `testTheDownloadNameIsTheSecondEncodedName`; `RbacTest::testFileGroupReadPolicies` gains an `OWNER_GOVERNED` branch (403 zero-grant, 404 for ADMIN) because the table's `null` no longer means open for any group; `CustomEntityGenericReadsTest` comments only.

## Residual F5 findings (reported, not fixed)

- Attaching: an MDE+STOCK_VIEW caller setting a product value to a battery-owned file still gets 403 (test passes).
- Detaching: the same caller can `PUT /api/userfields/batteries/{id}` with `""` (SetUserfields checks only MASTER_DATA_EDIT, not the owner's read permission or existence); the file then widens to the remaining owner. Asserted as current behaviour in `testResidualF5DetachingTheProtectedOwnerWidensTheRead` (passing test, not skipped, so the repository's skip detector stays quiet).
- Deleting the owning record cascades values (products, batteries, chores): same effect.
- Exclusive-create upload is an existence oracle for MDE holders; delete-then-reupload under a name replaces a protected file's bytes. Not tested.

## Compatibility and documentation

Wire change authorized by F1-F5: a caller who could read a userfile may now get 403. Parity scenario `.devtools/parity/harness/scenarios/60-users-files-calendar.js` is expected to diverge (upstream serves userfiles openly); not a gate. Stale text in `docs/adr/0035*` ("deliberately left open for now", for `userfiles`) is not edited here. `docs/security-sweep.md` ~:1077 stated `equipmentmanuals` is `null`, which was already stale (code maps it to EQUIPMENT_VIEW); I only added a sentence for `userfiles`.

Cost: the owner lookup scans `userfield_values` once per userfile request in PHP (no index; non-strict base64 variants cannot be prefiltered in SQL). Fine at household scale; the validator should measure it.

## Open questions

- None for the views: decided, see "Views and label entities" below. `label_*` / `print_*` are unchanged and need no decision.
- Pages that render userfield files under a leaf different from `EntityReadPolicy` for the owner (e.g. a master-data page) were not individually exercised; I found none in the views grep, but a validator pass over `userfields_tbody.blade.php` consumers is worthwhile.
- Owner-based write authorization (F5, #920) is not included.

## Views and label entities (maintainer decision, 2026-10-13)

> "Resolve via view key - look the owner up in the view by the same key GetObject uses (id; stock_id for stock) and apply the view's read permission; a view row that disappears makes the reference unresolved -> ADMIN only."

Implemented as `UserfileOwnerPolicy::OWNER_VIEWS`. Every view in `EntityReadPolicy::PERMISSIONS` (found by `information_schema.views`, pinned by a test) and its permission:

| View | Key | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| `stock_current_locations`, `products_last_purchased`, `products_average_price`, `quantity_unit_conversions_resolved`, `locations_resolved`, `product_groups_resolved`, `product_barcodes_view`, `product_groups_missing`, `product_location_missing`, `product_substitutions_resolved` | `id` | STOCK_VIEW |
| `uihelper_shopping_list` | `id` | SHOPPINGLIST_VIEW |
| `recipes_pos_resolved` | `id` | RECIPES_VIEW |

GetObject reads a view through `DB->{entity}($id)`, i.e. the `id` column; `testEveryLookedUpOwnerHasItsKeyColumn` asserts every looked-up table and view has it (it does, all twelve). Seven of the twelve views have a degenerate `id`: `stock_current_locations`, `products_last_purchased`, `products_average_price`, `product_substitutions_resolved`, `locations_resolved` and `product_groups_resolved` select a constant `1 AS id`; `quantity_unit_conversions_resolved` selects `-1` or `1`; and `product_barcodes_view` combines barcode and product ids, which can collide. For these the check is in effect "holds the view's read permission and the view has a row with that id": a reference to any other id is unresolved (ADMIN only), and emptying the view makes it unresolved too. This matches the maintainer decision as written and what GetObject returns for the same id; no caller gains more than the view's own permission. Maintainer note: files attached to these views are therefore not tied to one stock, location or product row. No view has a null permission. Nothing else in the rule changed: intersection across owners, definition rows ADMIN, `api_keys` nobody (a view row combined with either still behaves that way; tested).

`label_workers`, `label_drivers`, `label_worker_capabilities`, `label_printers`, `label_printer_status`, `label_templates`, `label_template_versions`, `label_assets`, `label_media_profiles`, `label_render_requests`, `print_jobs`, `print_attempts` and `print_evidence` are all `PERMISSION_ADMIN` in `EntityReadPolicy` (`testEveryLabelAndPrintEntityIsAdminOnly`). Treating a reference to one as unresolved is ADMIN only, which is exactly applying their policy, so behaviour is unchanged and this is no longer an open question. (`label_printer_status` is still looked up by `printer_id`.)

Out of scope here: `docs/adr/0048` on master still lists the views as an open question (its item 3); it should be updated by whoever owns the ADR.

## Validation round 1 (head 96f293e5)

- Blocking 1, derivative bypass: reproduced on ebf04429 first (`testReferencingADerivativeNeverWidensWhoMayReadIt`: `STOCK_VIEW alone, by the derivative name: expected a refusal / Failed asserting that 200 is identical to 403`; `testADerivativeNameFollowsTheOwnersOfItsOriginal` also differed). Fixed as above; the probe is now a test on both backends.
- Blocking 2, `roles` added, and `mqtt_product_entities`, which was the only other plain table in `EntityReadPolicy::PERMISSIONS` I could derive from `GetObject` (`DB->{entity}($id)`). Tests: both grant with their leaf and refuse without it.
- Left as unresolved (ADMIN only, treatment unchanged, for the maintainer to decide): the views (`stock_current_locations`, `products_last_purchased`, `products_average_price`, `quantity_unit_conversions_resolved`, `locations_resolved`, `product_groups_resolved`, `recipes_pos_resolved`, `product_barcodes_view`, `uihelper_shopping_list`, `product_groups_missing`, `product_location_missing`, `product_substitutions_resolved`) and the label/print tables (`label_workers`, `label_drivers`, `label_worker_capabilities`, `label_printers`, `print_*`, `label_templates` and the other `label_*`; their keys were not derived).
- Deleted definition rows: the join is now a LEFT JOIN and such a value is an unresolved reference (test added). Id range: 10-digit ids up to 2147483647 resolve (test with a user of that id).
- Maintainer-requested F3' tests, both backends: (a) a file referenced from a `userfields` row and from a `userentities` row gives a non-admin with every leaf but ADMIN neither bytes nor picture, and no derivative file or row is created; (b) ADMIN gets byte-identical bytes, and the picture derivative is created and served; (c) definition row + product: STOCK_VIEW refused, ADMIN 200; definition row + `api_keys`: ADMIN refused 403, and nobody else reads it.
- Phases after the last edit: storagefiles OK (98 tests, 917 assertions), rbac OK (114, 1293), householdpages OK (90, 697), stockpages OK (73, 674), labelapi OK (158, 2709), contract exit 0 (28 tests), openapidocument OK (15, 36), openapisecurity OK (11, 86), wirecontract OK (135, 4069).

## Validation round 2 (derivative chains)

- A derivative of a derivative still bypassed the root's owners (one suffix was stripped). Redesigned per the Opus review: chain normalisation to the root, root unreferenced is ADMIN only, every name in the chain only narrows, `OriginalOfDerivative` deleted, `FilesService::DerivativeName/DerivativeChain/RootOf` next to `DOWNSCALED_INFIX`, `GetStoredName` derives from `RootOf`. No write-side refusal of the infix (#920) and `userpictures` unchanged.
- Failing on 96f293e5 first (`storagefiles`: Tests: 113, Errors: 1, Failures: 14): the round-2 repro `testADerivativeOfAReferencedDerivativeDoesNotBypassTheRoot` ("STOCK_VIEW asking for x1__downscaledtoautox32__downscaledtoautox64.png: expected a refusal / Failed asserting that 200 is identical to 403"); `testAReferencedDerivativeNeedsTheRootsOwnersAsWell`; `testAPictureRequestNamingADerivativeDerivesFromTheRoot` ("has at most one derivative suffix / Failed asserting that 2 is equal to 1 or is less than 1"); `testAReferencedDerivativeOfAnUnreferencedRootIsAdminOnly`; also the chain-of-3, auto/mixed and display-name cases. The unit test errored on the missing helpers.
- New tests, both backends: round-2 repro, chain of three, auto and mixed sizes, display-name value for a derivative, D2 on a product with the root on a battery, picture request naming a derivative, referenced derivative of an unreferenced root; plus a unit test of `DerivativeName` / `RootOf` / `DerivativeChain` over sizes and names with `.`, `_` and a newline. One test of mine was wrong (it expected a shallower derivative to be narrowed by a deeper reference) and was corrected.
- All nine phases on the final head: storagefiles OK (113 tests, 1199 assertions), rbac OK (114, 1293), householdpages OK (90, 697), stockpages OK (73, 674), labelapi OK (158, 2709), contract exit 0 (28 tests), openapidocument OK (15, 36), openapisecurity OK (11, 86), wirecontract OK (135, 4069).
- `services/FilesService.php` is outside the original brief's file list; the design brief calls for it.

## Validation round 3 (userpictures)

- Applying `RootOf` in `GetStoredName` to every group opened a `userpictures` hole: a `USERS_EDIT_SELF` caller sets their own `picture_file_name` to `victim__downscaledto32x32.png` and, with `force_serve_as=picture`, got a fresh thumbnail of any victim's original. Two changes: `GetStoredName` reduces to the root only for `userfiles`; the own-picture read exception in `CheckGroupReadPermission` never applies to a name containing `FilesService::DOWNSCALED_INFIX`. The second also closes #941 (the already-cached derivative). Read path only.
- Failing on 82345356 first (`storagefiles`: Tests: 117, Failures: 4): `testTheOwnPictureExceptionNeverCreatesADerivativeForADerivativeName` ("a derivative name is not an own picture, and nothing is created for it / Failed asserting that 200 is identical to 403"), `testTheOwnPictureExceptionNeverServesACachedDerivativeOfSomeoneElsesPicture` ("the cached derivative is refused with it / Failed asserting that 200 is identical to 403"), and `testOnlyUserfilesDerivesFromTheRootOfADerivativeName` on both backends.
- New tests: (a) no derivative exists, nothing stored under the victim's prefix; (b) derivative cached by the victim's own request, refused with and without the option; (c) the caller's own avatar with force 32x32 still 200 without USERS_READ; (d) productpictures D1 with force 64: refused without STOCK_VIEW, 200 with it, derived from the name as asked; (e) userfiles D1 with force 64 stays covered by `testAPictureRequestNamingADerivativeDerivesFromTheRoot` (no name with two infixes). The subprocess helper `storagefiles-subprocess-helper.php` gained an optional JSON query argument for these.
- Phases on the final head: `[suite] phase=storagefiles exit=0` (117 tests, 1235 assertions), `rbac exit=0` (114, 1293), `householdpages exit=0` (90, 697), `stockpages exit=0` (73, 674), `labelapi exit=0` (158, 2709), `contract exit=0` (28 tests), `openapidocument exit=0` (15, 36), `openapisecurity exit=0` (11, 86), `wirecontract exit=0` (135, 4069).

## Revision 5 (views)

- Tests written first (unchanged policy, `storagefiles`, from `before-r5.log`): `Tests: 128, Assertions: ..., Failures: 5`. REGRESSION: `testAFileOnAViewRowFollowsThatViewsReadPermission` (both backends: `stock_current_locations: holding STOCK_VIEW / Failed asserting that 403 is identical to 200`), `testAViewOwnerAndATableOwnerBothHaveToAdmit` (both backends: `Failed asserting that 403 is identical to 200`), `testEveryViewWithAReadPolicyIsLookedUpByItsKey` (`Failed asserting that two arrays are identical` - the 12 views expected, `[]` actual). GUARD (pass before and after): `testAViewRowThatIsGoneMakesTheReferenceUnresolved`, `testAViewRowCombinedWithADefinitionOrApiKeyOwnerStillNarrows`, `testEveryLookedUpOwnerHasItsKeyColumn`, `testEveryLabelAndPrintEntityIsAdminOnly`.
- One existing test of mine encoded the old behaviour and was changed: `testDefinitionRowsAreAdminOnlyAndApiKeysAreReadByNobody` used `stock_current_locations` as the "policy but no lookup, unresolved" case; it now uses `label_workers`. After the fix it failed first on exactly that case (`stock_current_locations: a caller holding every leaf but ADMIN: expected a refusal / 200 is identical to 403`), as intended. The view test originally also used `products_last_purchased`, which has no rows in the fixture; replaced by `locations_resolved`.
- Fix: `UserfileOwnerPolicy::OWNER_VIEWS`, `OwnerExists` consults it, docblock and F1 comment updated. 2 files changed in the commit.
- Commit 0e9f9db9 (signed) and merge 6f9b2966 of origin/master 3ad3f401 (clean, signed). Phases on the merged head, all `exit=0`: storagefiles OK (128 tests, 1393 assertions), rbac OK (114, 1293), householdpages OK (90, 697), stockpages OK (76, 706), labelapi OK (174, 3454), contract OK (29 tests, 4 pre-existing deprecations), openapidocument OK (15, 36), openapisecurity OK (11, 86), wirecontract OK (135, 4085). Before the merge, on 0e9f9db9's policy, every phase also passed (the three non-storagefiles counts above are unchanged by it).

Fixes #941
Part of #905

## Independent validation of 6f9b2966 (coordinator note)

Opus security review, VALIDATED WITH NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATIONS. Re-probed through the HTTP stack: the 12 refusals are identical; orphan and dangling definition rows are ADMIN only; view+view, view+table and view+definition/api_keys are intersections; derivative chains of 2 and 3 need the root's owners; a refused picture request on a view owner created nothing in the store; own avatar 200, another user's picture 403, every #941 probe 403 with nothing created; userfiles on /stockoverview, /stockentries, /locations and /batteriesoverview serve 200; productpictures as on master. Revert (policy from 45aa7a53, storagefiles): `Tests: 128, Assertions: 1325, Failures: 5` with the three REGRESSION tests listed above. All nine phases exit 0 (storagefiles 137 tests with 9 probe tests, rbac 114/1293, householdpages 90/697, stockpages 76/706, labelapi 174/3454, contract 29/79, openapidocument 15/36, openapisecurity 11/86, wirecontract 135/4085).

Known test limitation: `testAViewRowThatIsGoneMakesTheReferenceUnresolved` references id 999999, which never existed, so it pins "unknown id is unresolved" but does not delete a real view row. The validator's probe did (deleting a `recipes_pos` row took `recipes_pos_resolved` from 200 to 403 for RECIPES_VIEW; emptying stock took `stock_current_locations` to 403 for STOCK_VIEW, ADMIN 200).

Out of scope, not edited here: Proposed ADR-0048's open question 3 still says this PR makes view-owned files ADMIN only, which the 2026-10-13 view decision superseded. `SetUserfields` accepts values at view ids that do not exist (204); that is write-side, #920.
